c.tagline: Britain's harbourside capital of street art, music, and maker culture.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed Hackney cabs are metered and can be hailed or found at ranks; private-hire cars must be pre-booked. Uber and Bolt operate citywide.

emergency.note: Dial 999 for police, fire, or ambulance; use NHS 111 for urgent but non-life-threatening medical advice.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The Harbourside and Park Street bar areas get rowdy late, and Stokes Croft/St Pauls warrant awareness after dark.

hood_desc: The revitalised waterfront at the heart of the city, ringed by the M Shed and We The Curious museums, the SS Great Britain, and quayside bars and restaurants; the central, walkable base for a first visit.
The genteel Georgian hilltop village above the Avon Gorge, famous for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, crescents of pale stone, antique shops, and the zoo; scenic and refined.
The raw, creative artery north of the centre, plastered with murals (including Banksy's), lined with independent cafes, record shops, and some of the city's edgiest nightlife.
The medieval commercial core around cobbled King Street, home to the Old Vic theatre, centuries-old pubs, and the covered St Nicholas Market; lively and full of history.
The up-and-coming, family-friendly quarters south of the harbour, centred on North Street's independent shops, the Tobacco Factory, and street-art murals; laid-back and local.
lodging: Mercure Bristol Holland House Hotel & Spa

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the UK.

transit.hours: Buses run from around 5:00am to about 11:30pm on core routes, with limited night services at weekends; the harbour ferry runs mainly in daylight hours.
transit.note: Bristol Ferry Boats hop between harbourside piers (Temple Meads, city centre, SS Great Britain, Hotwells) — as much a scenic ride as everyday transport.
transit.pay: Bristol has no metro or tram; First Bus runs most services — tap a contactless card or pay the driver, with a daily fare cap, or buy an mTicket (a day ticket is about £5) in the First Bus app. MetroBus rapid routes use off-bus ticket machines. Local trains from Temple Meads serve the wider area.

transit.m: Bristol Airport Flyer (A1) bus to Temple Meads & city centre (~30 min, every 10-20 min)

tip.r: ~10-12.5% at restaurants if a service charge isn't already added; no need to tip when ordering at the bar in a pub.
